name: C++ profile: reuse-store tasks, set B
about: Thirteen new questions about the sound-design C++ enforcement profile, none answered by set A (reuse-tasks-c++.json). Set B, with set A, builds the store for Test 1 (what reuse buys, including whether it prevents the out-of-memory failure): different questions over the same files as Test 1's measured tasks. Run against set A's store, it also shows the overlap gradient on small tasks. Every task carries an overlap tag saying how its answer relates to what set A's tasks read: same-section (the answer sits in a table or section an A task needed), same-file (a different section of a file an A task read), new-file (a file no A task needed). Scoring is as in set A: every group in expect must be matched by one of its alternatives (substring; case-insensitive unless caseSensitive).
sourceNote: Candidates relative to this file, first existing wins: the first for the copy in sound-design's enforcement/languages/bechmarking, the second for the copy in linux's ubuntu/26.04/05-llm-local, the third for the copy in the llama.cpp fork's bench/ (each with sound-design cloned beside it). --source overrides.
